chosen_dimensions: whether retrieval is the primary evaluated task
rationale: These three dimensions are exactly what BEIR's own gap argument turns on (Section 2): prior broad evaluations are narrow in task coverage, treat retrieval as secondary, and use small corpora that structurally favor one architecture family.

matrix_prior_benchmarks.problem_framing: cross-domain evaluation of sentence-level answer retrieval for question answering
matrix_prior_benchmarks.method_family: n/a (an evaluation suite, not a retrieval method)
matrix_prior_benchmarks.key_assumption: one task type (QA) generalizes to represent retrieval broadly
matrix_prior_benchmarks.data_eval: 8 QA datasets; 5/8 Wikipedia-based; 6/8 with fewer than 100k candidate sentences
matrix_prior_benchmarks.weakness_limit: single task type; small corpora, a scale reported (via SRC-054) to favor dense over lexical retrieval
matrix_prior_benchmarks.relation_to_beir: BEIR extends coverage from 1 task/8 datasets to 9 tasks/18 datasets and reports large-corpus results, avoiding the small-corpus advantage for dense methods

matrix_prior_benchmarks.problem_framing: benchmark for knowledge-intensive language tasks (of which retrieval is one component)
matrix_prior_benchmarks.key_assumption: Wikipedia is a sufficient retrieval corpus for knowledge-intensive tasks
matrix_prior_benchmarks.data_eval: 5 tasks / 11 datasets, all retrieving only from Wikipedia; retrieval is not the primary evaluated task
matrix_prior_benchmarks.strength: large task variety within knowledge-intensive NLP
matrix_prior_benchmarks.weakness_limit: single domain (Wikipedia); retrieval quality is not the object of evaluation
matrix_prior_benchmarks.relation_to_beir: BEIR isolates retrieval itself as the object of evaluation and spans domains beyond Wikipedia (bio-medical, finance, Twitter, news, argumentation, community forums)

matrix_architecture_families.problem_framing: rank documents by lexical overlap with the query
matrix_architecture_families.key_assumption: query terms present in relevant documents (bag-of-words)
matrix_architecture_families.strength: no training needed; used in BEIR as the reference baseline
matrix_architecture_families.weakness_limit: lexical gap: misses relevant documents with no shared vocabulary
matrix_architecture_families.relation_to_beir: the one system evaluated in every BEIR dataset as the comparison point

matrix_architecture_families.source: SRC-011 (DeepCT, Dai and Callan, 2020); SRC-079 (SPARTA, Zhao et al., 2021)
matrix_architecture_families.problem_framing: learn term weights/representations on top of lexical matching
matrix_architecture_families.key_assumption: a BERT-learned term-weighting/expansion signal transfers across domains
matrix_architecture_families.weakness_limit: BEIR finds both underperform BM25 on nearly all 18 zero-shot datasets

matrix_architecture_families.problem_framing: expand documents with model-generated queries, then rank lexically
matrix_architecture_families.key_assumption: a generative model can add domain-appropriate vocabulary a lexical matcher would otherwise miss
matrix_architecture_families.data_eval: T5 trained on MS MARCO, applied to generate 40 queries/document per target dataset
matrix_architecture_families.strength: BEIR finds it one of the few systems that generalizes well (beats BM25 on 11/18)

matrix_architecture_families.source: SRC-031 (DPR, Karpukhin et al., 2020); SRC-073 (ANCE, Xiong et al., 2020); SRC-023 (TAS-B, Hofstatter et al., 2021)
matrix_architecture_families.problem_framing: map queries/documents to a shared dense vector space
matrix_architecture_families.key_assumption: a single learned vector captures the semantics needed for matching across domains
matrix_architecture_families.data_eval: trained on MS MARCO (ANCE, TAS-B) or 4 QA datasets (DPR)
matrix_architecture_families.strength: can capture semantic matches beyond shared vocabulary
matrix_architecture_families.weakness_limit: BEIR finds all three underperform BM25 on average zero-shot, DPR most severely

matrix_architecture_families.problem_framing: keep token-level representations and compare them at query time
matrix_architecture_families.key_assumption: preserving fine-grained token interactions improves transfer over single-vector compression
matrix_architecture_families.weakness_limit: large index (multiple vectors per document); still underperforms BM25 on 9/18 datasets

matrix_architecture_families.source: SRC-070 (MiniLM cross-encoder re-ranker, Wang et al., 2020), used as BM25+CE
matrix_architecture_families.problem_framing: re-score a first-stage candidate list with full cross-attention between query and document
matrix_architecture_families.key_assumption: cross-attention over the full query-document pair, applied only to a short candidate list, is affordable and effective
matrix_architecture_families.data_eval: trained on MS MARCO via knowledge distillation
matrix_architecture_families.strength: BEIR's best average zero-shot performance (+11% vs BM25, beats it on 16/18)
matrix_architecture_families.weakness_limit: highest per-query latency (>350ms) of all systems compared
